title: say_due_goodbyes leaves ScreenClient::GoodbyesDue forever when no client is on screen, so the next connect loops without opening
trigger: Log out / delete account / disk-full runs close_screen_client: screen_leaves_later sets GoodbyesDue, then take_live empties live in the same update. The deferred say_due_goodbyes sees live.is_none(), calls end_account_surfaces and returns without setting client back to Empty. The next sign-in/connect (connect_ui.rs:311) then sees goodbyes_due() true on every pass and returns true to loop again, never reaching open_prepared
effect: After logout (or full disk) the next connect stays on Connecting forever and spins the wake loop; needs an app restart. Debug builds also trip the put_on_screen debug_assert on the switch path
fix: say_due_goodbyes sets client = Empty after end_account_surfaces (every exit of GoodbyesDue leaves it)

title: Scope and reaction notification edits send the whole settings struct copied from the session mirror, so two quick edits lose the first
trigger: Open Notifications defaults, flip Preview then Mentions (or Message reactions then Story reactions) before TDLib echoes updateScopeNotificationSettings / updateReactionNotificationSettings. Each apply_* clones the mirror, changes one field and sends the full struct (setScopeNotificationSettings is whole-object)
effect: The second send carries the stale value of the first field, so the first change is silently reverted on the server and the switch snaps back when the echo arrives
fix: one in-flight edit per scope held as a stage (Fetch/Saving with request id) and the next edit based on the pending value

title: App-wide desktop notifications switch is written only to clients that are live when it is toggled
trigger: Turn Desktop notifications off (settings or tray) while an account has no running client (not on screen, not in the background set); later that account connects: live.rs:261 loads its own prefs file, where the flag is still true
effect: The account notifies again although the user disabled notifications app-wide
fix: one app-level value read by every session (owned by the app), not a per-account copy kept in step by hand
